name: Toufik Torche
detail: FLN Deputy and Chairman of the APN Finance and Budget Committee in 2017; led the committee vote to delete the Impôt sur la fortune from the 2018 Finance Bill, arguing the project was 'stillborn' and would encourage informality and capital flight abroad.

name: Forum des Chefs d'Entreprises (FCE) / Ali Haddad
detail: Principal Algerian employers' organization (rebranded CREA) led until 2019 by businessman Ali Haddad; lobbied against the 2018 Impôt sur la fortune, arguing that productive assets should be exempt and warning of investor deterrence.

name: Chafaâ Bouaiche
detail: Former FFS Parliamentary Group Leader and Deputy for Béjaïa who criticized the government's withdrawal of the wealth tax in PLF 2018; died on 28 July 2021.

name: Abderrahmane Benkhalfa
detail: Former Minister of Finance (2015–2016) who commented on tax reform and opposed a standalone wealth tax during the 2016–2017 budget debates; died on 23 April 2021.

name: Karim Djoudi
detail: Former Minister of Finance (2007–2014) involved in earlier property tax (impôt sur le patrimoine) debates; died on 13 May 2022.

name: Abderrahmane Mebtoul
detail: Economist and former Court of Accounts member; published extensive analyses on the Impôt sur la fortune warning that without a reliable information system and formalization of the parallel economy the tax is inapplicable and risks perverse effects.

name: Achour Idir
detail: National Coordinator and spokesperson of the Conseil des Lycées d'Algérie (CLA) and leader of the Autonomous Unions' Intersyndicale; publicly denounced the APN Finance Committee's cancellation of the Impôt sur la fortune in November 2017, but died on 4 April 2019 (his union CLA is recorded as A0025).

name: Soufiane Djilali
detail: President of the Jil Jadid party; dismissed the government's 2017 wealth tax proposal as a 'demagogic decision to win people's emotions' without advocating a domestic net wealth tax himself.

name: Rassemblement pour la Culture et la Démocratie (RCD)
detail: Secular opposition party; while its deputies boycotted the PLF 2018 vote, its official May 2020 statement on the Supplementary Finance Law dismissed the newly enacted Impôt sur la fortune as 'populist in nature insofar as no serious registry exists to tax the rich' without endorsing a wealth tax proposal of its own.

name: Fares Mesdour
detail: Economist and university lecturer; argued in October 2017 that imposing a statutory wealth tax in Algeria would encourage tax evasion in the absence of a property-declaration culture and advocated voluntary Islamic zakat funds as an alternative.

name: Abdelkader Berriche
detail: Economic analyst and former Member of the People's National Assembly; commented on the administrative hurdles and lack of a national property database facing the 2020 wealth tax without expressing normative support.

name: Mahfoud Kaoubi
detail: Economist and university lecturer (محفوظ كاوبي); argued in El Mostathmir (December 2022) that the wealth tax is a 'double-edged sword' (سلاح ذو حدين) with marginal revenue yield globally and claimed that its application in France caused companies and capital to flee to Luxembourg and Belgium.

name: Abdelhamid Bouallag / Syndicat Autonome des Fonctionnaires des Impôts (SAFI)
detail: Secretary General of the Autonomous Union of Tax Officials (SAFI); called in December 2021 for a radical overhaul of the tax code to achieve 'fiscal equity' and end Algeria's status as a 'tax haven' where 90% of tax files remain unregularized, without explicitly proposing or naming a net wealth tax.

name: Nabil Djemaa
detail: Asks for a database and digitisation; does not state support for the tax.

name: Amel Abdellatif
detail: Describes a cadastral data-sharing programme, not a statement about the wealth tax itself.

name: Direction Générale des Impôts
detail: Anti-fraud audit powers across several taxes; no wealth-tax statement by the organisation.

name: Maghreb Émergent
detail: Outlet complains about missing statistics; not a statement of support.

name: Lynda Nacer
detail: Journalist complains about missing statistics; not a statement of support.

name: Tarek Tridi
detail: Quote narrates what deputies said at a hearing he chaired; not his own words.
